tasks.title: Pod tab: collapse the working indicator into the status dot
acceptance: `PodTab.tsx` no longer mounts `<WorkingIndicator />` and no longer imports `../activity`. A running Pod's tab renders exactly ONE element matching `[data-status]` inside `pod-tab:<podId>`; `PodTab.test.tsx` asserts that count is 1 for every one of the five `PodStatus` values. Do not delete anything under `src/renderer/src/activity/` — T3 owns that.

The status dot's markup is otherwise unchanged: it still carries `data-status={status}` and the inline `--pod-status-color` from `statusToken(status)`, it gains no new prop, no new class read from script, no test id, no accessible name and no text. Motion is derived from the status the tab ALREADY carries, per the frontend discipline's rule that a presentational component takes data and nothing else.

`PodBar.module.css` declares `@keyframes ocStatusPulse` with the body pinned in `contracts/status-dot-motion.ts` section 2, and applies it as `animation: ocStatusPulse 1.4s ease-in-out infinite` on the selector `.statusDot[data-status='running']` and on no other selector. The base `.statusDot` rule sets no `animation`. `PodBar.styles.test.ts` asserts both, by exact selector, using the file's existing `ruleFor()` helper.

`PodBar.module.css` carries a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block setting `animation: none` on that same selector and changing nothing else — the re-homed guard from the deleted `activity/WorkingIndicator.styles.test.ts` (contract `activity-module-retirement.ts` section 4). `PodBar.styles.test.ts` asserts the query is present, that `animation: none` falls inside it and not in a later rule, and that the reduced-motion branch introduces no `display: none`, no `visibility: hidden` and no `opacity: 0` — the dot keeps its size, shape and hue when motion is off.

The `idle` dot is sharpened to a hollow ring at the idle hue: `.statusDot[data-status='idle']` keeps `background: transparent` and gains `border-width: var(--oc-border-thick)`. Its hue still comes from `--pod-status-color`, which `statusToken('idle')` already resolves to `--oc-status-idle`; no new token is introduced and `--oc-status-idle` is not recoloured. `PodBar.styles.test.ts` asserts the rule by exact selector. The `waiting` halo, the `beached` square and the `closed` flat-bar rules are byte-unchanged — assert each still declares what it declares today.

Colour is never the only carrier (frontend discipline, accessibility floor): the `srOnly` sentence still opens with `STATUS_LABEL[status]` verbatim, for all five statuses. `PodTab.test.tsx` asserts the status word is in `container.textContent` in the same render as every dot assertion, and the existing `STATUS_WORD` map stays duplicated in the test rather than imported, for the reason its own comment gives.

The three assertion sites that named the retired test id — `PodTab.test.tsx` lines around 341, 353 and 368 (`screen.getByTestId(WORKING_INDICATOR_TEST_ID)`, `dot?.nextElementSibling`, `queryByTestId(...)`) — are REPLACED by dot assertions, not deleted. The 'renders NO indicator for a %s Pod' case becomes 'renders exactly one status dot, in the %s state, and no second mark beside it'; the adjacency case becomes an assertion that the dot has no sibling mark. The import of `WORKING_INDICATOR_TEST_ID` is removed. Test names state the condition and the expected outcome (test discipline, Naming).

NEW FILE `src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.source.test.ts` re-homes the source guard from the deleted `activity/WorkingIndicator.source.test.ts` (contract `activity-module-retirement.ts` section 3): reading `./PodTab.tsx?raw`, it asserts the source names none of `setInterval`, `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `Date.now`, and none of `../activity`, `WorkingIndicator`, `WORKING_INDICATOR_TEST_ID`. It must NOT copy `LaneRow.source.test.ts`'s `useState|useEffect|useRef` assertion — `PodTab.tsx` legitimately uses `useEffect` and `useRef` for the delete-control focus rescue. It opens with the vacuity guard (`typeof source === 'string'`, non-empty, contains `function PodTab`) so it cannot pass against a blank read. Do NOT add a second `declare module '*.tsx?raw'`; `activity/raw.d.ts` still supplies it and T3 moves it.

Every new or changed test in this task was SEEN FAILING before the code that satisfies it existed (test discipline, Coverage). The report names, per test, the command run and the failure message observed. 'Verified by inspection' is not evidence. Command, verbatim, from the repository root, with no NODE_PATH and no scratch vitest config: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs" run src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.test.tsx src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.source.test.ts src/renderer/src/pods/PodBar.styles.test.ts

DO NOT claim the animation runs on the strength of a jsdom or a text assertion. Vitest resolves `*.module.css` to a blanked module and jsdom applies no stylesheet, so neither can see motion. The declaration-level proof above is this task's share; the proof that the emitted animation name actually RESOLVES is T3 criterion 4, which covers both surfaces after both stylesheets are final. If you choose to run the build yourself as well, note that T2 may be building the same `out/` concurrently — re-run once on a torn read rather than reporting a failure.

The whole pods suite and the web typecheck are green and were observed, not assumed: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs" run src/renderer/src/pods, and node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc" --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json --composite false exits 0. `PodBar.module.css` still hardcodes no colour and uses only tokens named in the frozen `TOKENS` map, with no `!important` and no `outline: none` — the four existing assertions at the top of `PodBar.styles.test.ts` still pass unrelaxed.

tasks.title: Lane rail: collapse the working indicator into the status dot
acceptance: `LaneRow.tsx` no longer mounts `<WorkingIndicator />` and no longer imports `../activity`. A running lane's `.meta` line renders exactly ONE mark — the existing `.dot` inside `.status` — and no sibling indicator; `LaneRail.test.tsx` asserts that for all four `LaneStatus` values. The row stays `memo`-wrapped and keeps its existing docblock claim that it holds no clock. Do not delete anything under `src/renderer/src/activity/` — T3 owns that.

`LANE_STATUS_LABEL` in `lanes/lane-status.ts` is NOT touched, and no `Active` or `Waiting` vocabulary is added anywhere on the lane row. The lane already renders a word for each of its four statuses; the reviewer should treat any new status vocabulary as a blocking finding. `lane-status.ts` is outside this task's `owns` set — if you believe it needs a change, stop and escalate.

The dot's markup is unchanged: still `<span className={styles.dot} aria-hidden="true" />` with no new prop, no new class read from script, no test id and no text. Motion is derived from `row.status`, which the enclosing `.status` span already carries as `data-status`, per the frontend discipline's rule that a presentation component takes data and nothing else.

`LaneRail.module.css` declares `@keyframes ocStatusPulse` with the body pinned in `contracts/status-dot-motion.ts` section 2, and applies it as `animation: ocStatusPulse 1.4s ease-in-out infinite` on the selector `.status[data-status='running'] .dot` and on no other selector. The base `.dot` rule sets no `animation`, and the four `.status[data-status='…'] .dot` hue rules keep their current backgrounds unchanged. `LaneRail.styles.test.ts` asserts all of this by exact selector.

`LaneRail.module.css` carries a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block setting `animation: none` on that same selector and changing nothing else — the re-homed guard from the deleted `activity/WorkingIndicator.styles.test.ts` (contract `activity-module-retirement.ts` section 4). `LaneRail.styles.test.ts` asserts the query is present, that `animation: none` falls inside it rather than in a later rule, and that the reduced-motion branch introduces no `display: none`, no `visibility: hidden` and no `opacity: 0`.

Colour is never the only carrier (frontend discipline, accessibility floor): every dot assertion in `LaneRail.test.tsx` asserts `LANE_STATUS_LABEL[status]` is in the row's `textContent` in the same render, exactly as the two existing indicator tests already do. `.awaiting` / `.awaitingDot` are untouched.

The three assertion sites that named the retired test id — `LaneRail.test.tsx` line 6 (the import), 469 and 493 — are REPLACED by dot assertions, not deleted. The 'mounts the indicator on a running lane' case becomes an assertion that the running row's `.meta` line holds the status dot, the status word and no second mark; the 'mounts NO indicator on a %s lane' cases become assertions that a done, orphaned or stopped row holds the same single dot and its word. Test names state the condition and the expected outcome (test discipline, Naming).

`LaneRow.source.test.ts` keeps its existing four-primitive block (`setInterval`, `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `Date.now`) and its `useState|useEffect|useRef` block unchanged — that is the re-homed 'nothing here schedules a frame' guard for this surface — and GAINS assertions that the source contains none of `../activity`, `WorkingIndicator`, `WORKING_INDICATOR_TEST_ID`. Its docblock reference to `activity/raw.d.ts` is corrected to `styles/raw.d.ts`, the new home T3 creates; a comment pointing at a deleted file is a trap for the next reader. Do NOT add a second `declare module '*.tsx?raw'`.

Every new or changed test in this task was SEEN FAILING before the code that satisfies it existed (test discipline, Coverage). The report names, per test, the command run and the failure message observed. Command, verbatim, from the repository root, with no NODE_PATH and no scratch vitest config: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs" run src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.test.tsx src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRow.source.test.ts src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.styles.test.ts

DO NOT claim the animation runs on the strength of a jsdom or a text assertion. Vitest resolves `*.module.css` to a blanked module and jsdom applies no stylesheet, so neither can see motion. The declaration-level proof above is this task's share; the proof that the emitted animation name actually RESOLVES is T3 criterion 4. If you run the build yourself as well, T1 may be building the same `out/` concurrently — re-run once on a torn read rather than reporting a failure.

The whole lanes suite and the web typecheck are green and were observed, not assumed: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs" run src/renderer/src/lanes, and node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc" --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json --composite false exits 0. `LaneRail.module.css` still hardcodes no colour and uses only tokens named in the frozen `TOKENS` map, with no `!important` and no `outline: none`; `LaneRail.styles.test.ts`'s existing assertions still pass unrelaxed. `LaneRail.test.tsx`'s existing no-timer assertions (`vi.getTimerCount()` zero, the Profiler re-render check) still pass.

tasks.title: Retire the activity module, re-home its ambient declaration, and guard the two pulse definitions against drift
acceptance: All seven files listed in `contracts/activity-module-retirement.ts` section 1 are deleted and the `src/renderer/src/activity/` directory no longer exists. Before deleting, re-run the content search that justifies it and REPORT ITS OUTPUT: a search of `src/` for `WorkingIndicator`, `WORKING_INDICATOR_TEST_ID`, `working-indicator` and `from '../activity'` must return no hit outside the directory being deleted. If it returns one, stop and escalate — T1 or T2 left an importer behind.

NEW FILE `src/renderer/src/styles/raw.d.ts` carries the ambient `declare module '*.tsx?raw'` block moved from `activity/raw.d.ts`, with a docblock stating why it is a Vite text import and not `node:fs` (no file under `src/renderer/**` may import a `node:` builtin; `tsconfig.web.json` sets `"types": []` so that it cannot). It is created in the SAME task as the deletion, so the declaration never exists twice at once. It is NOT added to `styles/css.d.ts`, which is about CSS and is referenced by name in three docblocks.

The web typecheck is green and was OBSERVED, not assumed — it is the only check that can catch a missing `*.tsx?raw` declaration, because Vite resolves the import at runtime regardless and a green Vitest run is therefore not evidence: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc" --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json --composite false exits 0. Prove the check can fail: temporarily rename `styles/raw.d.ts`, observe the typecheck failing in `LaneRow.source.test.ts` and `PodTab.source.test.ts`, report the error text, then restore it.

THE ANIMATION IS PROVED TO RESOLVE IN THE EMITTED BUNDLE, for BOTH modules. This is the one failure mode no suite in this repository can see — a module referencing a keyframe name that does not exist emits a hashed reference to nothing and the dot silently never moves. Run node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/electron-vite/bin/electron-vite.js" build, read the emitted renderer CSS under `out/renderer/assets/`, and report the literal matched strings showing that, for each of the two module scopes independently, an `@keyframes _ocStatusPulse_<hash>` is emitted AND an `animation:` declaration names that same `_ocStatusPulse_<hash>` string. Two different hashes — one per file — is the EXPECTED result and is not drift. A hash present on one side and absent on the other is the falsified shape from the session log: stop and escalate rather than improvising a second mechanism. Quote the grep or search command that produced the match; do not assert a count you did not run.

NEW FILE `src/renderer/src/styles/status-motion.styles.test.ts` is the drift guard the per-module shape requires. Reading `../pods/PodBar.module.css#?raw` and `../lanes/LaneRail.module.css#?raw` — the `#?raw` spelling, per the note on `*.css#?raw` in `styles/css.d.ts`, which must not be 'tidied' to `?raw` — it asserts that both files declare a `@keyframes ocStatusPulse`, that the two keyframe BODIES are identical after whitespace normalisation, that both apply the shorthand tail `1.4s ease-in-out infinite`, and that both carry a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block setting `animation: none`. It opens with the vacuity guard both existing styles tests use, so it cannot pass against a blank read.

The drift guard RE-TYPES its expected keyframe text rather than importing it from either stylesheet or from the session contract — a test that derived its expectation from the thing under test would pass while both files drifted together. This is the reason `PodTab.test.tsx` already states for duplicating `STATUS_WORD`, and it is a blocking finding if the test computes its expectation from one file and compares it to the other alone.

The drift guard is SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL (test discipline, Coverage): inject the drift — change one file's keyframe body, or its duration, or delete one reduced-motion block — observe the guard failing, report the failure message, then revert the injection. A drift test never seen failing has not been shown to detect drift.
Test names state the condition and the expected outcome (test discipline, Naming); no name says 'works' or 'is correct', and no name claims more than its assertions check.

The full suite is green and was observed, not assumed: node "C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs" run. Report the pass count from that run's own output. No test file remains that imports the deleted directory, and no test was deleted rather than re-homed — the report accounts for each of the three deleted suites (`WorkingIndicator.test.tsx`, `.source.test.ts`, `.styles.test.ts`) by naming which of the criteria in T1, T2 or T3 now carries each of its obligations, or by stating that the obligation went with the component it tested.
